scenario: Migration and preservation proof for legacy writers and typed commands
expected_result: The gate fails if any set, legacy or typed, is lost. Scenarios: (1) a legacy device holds a pending whole-document `.set` for session S while a typed command for S converts S; the legacy write then flushes: it is accepted into the projection, the trigger copies it to the quarantine, the projection is regenerated, the typed sets are intact, `quarantineCount` is 1 and the app shows the review prompt; nothing is lost. (2) Reverse order: legacy write lands first, typed command converts it: legacy sets are `LEGACY_UNVERIFIED`, a typed APPEND at the same slot returns `DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_SET`, no set doubled. (3) Dormant old installation: an old build, offline, holds a queued legacy write for S; typed conversion of S happens; the old device reconnects 100 days later (account in `DRAIN` or `SERVER_ONLY`): the write is preserved in the quarantine and visible to the user. (4) `SEALED` is refused by the sealing tool unless its preconditions hold; with `SEALED` set, a client write is denied and the test records the exact cohort of O-R1; no scenario may lose a write while the state is not `SEALED`. (5) A typed command from a device not in `drainedDevices` returns `MIGRATION_HOLD`, stays queued, applies after the ack; a reinstall acks immediately. (6) `sendingPaused = true`: 15 commands accepted and kept, none applied; the DRAIN clock does not advance while paused and a cutover attempt at day 30 of calendar time with 5 paused days is refused; after unpausing 15 sets exist once each. (7) Cutover: at 30 unpaused days with one device seen in the last 90 days that has not acked a flush, the account stays in `DRAIN` (no deadline moves it); after that device acks, it moves to `SERVER_ONLY`. (8) Attempted state regression is refused. (9) Trigger failure then retry: the quarantine copy exists exactly once (idempotent id) and the count rose once, the projection is repaired, and the backlog alert fires when older than 15 minutes. (10) A legacy write racing a typed apply (overwritten on the projection before the repair) is still quarantined from its event snapshot. (11) Late legacy delete: a legacy DELETE is produced offline, newer typed sets are then COMMITTED from another device, the DELETE is delivered: the typed session and every newer set survive, the delete is quarantined as a deletion intent, the projection is repaired, and only an explicit deleteWorkoutSession with the current expectedSessionGeneration and expectedRevision deletes (a stale value of either returns STALE_DELETE). ABA: observe generation 1 / revision 5, capture a delete request, delete and explicitly recreate generation 2, advance it to revision 5, deliver the old request: the new session and all its sets survive. (13) Tombstone before conversion and legacy delete: delete generation 1 through the callable (tombstone), deliver a late legacy .set for the same id, then a typed command of generation 1: the answer is SESSION_DELETED_ELSEWHERE, no typed session exists, the legacy content exists only as a POST_DELETE_WRITE quarantine entry and the projection is removed. Legacy delete of an unconverted session: commit a legacy DELETE, force the trigger to run late, commit a stale .set and then a typed conversion in between: the result is exactly one typed session, a pending DELETE_INTENT and no lost set; the workout is deleted only by the owner's confirmed deleteWorkoutSession. (14) Forged provenance: a client writes projectionRevision equal to the current revision, a copied old projectionSeal with changed content, a forged completed set or a stale revision to the projection: rules deny client-created or client-changed server-owned fields, and a write that still lands fails seal verification, is quarantined and repaired; authoritative views never show it. (15) Once-per-event count and convergence: interleave typed commits, quarantine creation, repair, acknowledgement loss and repeated trigger delivery, with fault injection before and after each write of the trigger transaction; after convergence there is exactly one entry per genuine legacy event, quarantineCount and unresolvedTotal equal the number of unresolved entries, the projection equals the latest typed state, and replaying repair events creates no entry. (16) Delayed genuine events: commit two consecutive typed revisions and deliver their projection events in reverse order and repeatedly: both verify as server writes, zero entries, zero increment. (17) Post-delete discovery: delete a session, upload a late legacy snapshot and never open that session id: the owner finds the entry in the account-level inventory and can export or dismiss it, no typed session or canonical workout appears, and a reader hides the restored projection during the repair window. (18) Session classes: in SERVER_ONLY deliver legacy create, update and delete events for a converted session (A), a deleted session (B) and a never-seen session (C); each follows exactly its outcome of protocol 8.3 item 10 and no accepted data is silently discarded. Divergence and stale delete: two old clients write divergent whole-document snapshots (set E1, and E2 without E1) to a session that is not yet converted, delivered in both orders with trigger delays and retries, with the trigger conversion and a typed conversion racing in any order: E1 and E2 both survive, one in typed state and the other as a quarantine entry, until the owner resolves them. A legacy DELETE queued on device A, a newer set E2 committed on device B, then A's DELETE flushed and both triggers replayed in either order: E2 stays and a deletion intent is pending. Export without any typed command: the account export contains every unresolved quarantine entry. Backfill: entering DRAIN with a session that no typed command ever touched converts it before DRAIN starts. (19) Summary and head protection: with unresolved entries present, owner-authenticated create, update and delete of workout_quarantine_summary and workout_session_heads documents are all rejected and the recovery prompt stays correct. (20) Reader trust: seed a converted session, a deleted session and ten legacy sessions never touched by a typed command, then upgrade the client and enter DRAIN with no typed mutation: the ten appear in history, progress and export with provenance LEGACY_UNVERIFIED, the deleted one is absent; then hold the repair trigger and write a stale or forged projection over a converted session: its contents are not shown as committed facts (the head check fails) and after repair the latest typed state is shown. (21) DELETE provenance: deliver a server DELETE and a delayed legacy DELETE against a tombstoned session, reversed and duplicated: the server deletion creates no entry; a legacy DELETE against a converted session creates one deletion intent exactly once. Also: server DELETE of generation 1, explicit recreate as generation 2, then delayed and duplicated delivery of the generation 1 DELETE event: no deletion intent for generation 2 and the new workout is unchanged; repeat after a legacy whole-document .set stripped the server fields of the generation 1 projection before the authoritative delete (the createTime recorded in the tombstone deletes list identifies the deleted incarnation exactly). Then, for one session id, two runs with ONE deterministic expectation each: run A, before.createTime available: server DELETE of generation 1, recreate generation 2, a separate legacy DELETE with a stripped before-image, events reversed and with near-identical timestamps: the server deletion is a no-op and the legacy deletion produces exactly one deletion intent. Run B, before.createTime unavailable: BOTH deletions each produce exactly one visible deletion intent (the conservative outcome), no workout is deleted automatically, and a deploy check that the pinned SDK exposes before.createTime fails closed, keeping the trigger path disabled when it does not. (22) Backfill boundary: run the last pass of the clean scan, then commit a new legacy CREATE and, separately, an overwrite of an already converted session, and hold their triggers until after the compare-and-set that sets phase OPEN: OPEN certifies only the documents that existed at the start of the clean scan (the check reports no claim about later events), neither write is ever left outside typed state or quarantine once its trigger or the next typed command runs, the session shows "verifying" meanwhile, and the SERVER_ONLY cutover is refused while the trigger backlog alert has fired in the last 24 hours. (23) Writerless sessions: backfill a legacy session and trigger-convert a new one; a new client's first typed item claims each (same deterministic result for both), a second device is refused with NOT_WRITER and an explicit takeover then succeeds with the new epoch. (24) Idempotent conversion: deliver one legacy CREATE event ten times, including a crash after the conversion commit and before the trigger acknowledgement: one typed session, no quarantine entry, unchanged counters, one head. Marker expiry: process E as CONVERTED, change the typed session, delete the marker as if by TTL, redeliver E: zero new quarantine entries, unchanged counters and canonical state (the permanent convertedFromEventId and quarantine ids decide); repeat for an event that ended QUARANTINED and was then resolved (the permanent entry is found before any create: same resolved status, one entry, unchanged quarantineCount and unresolvedTotal, no new user task) and for one that is still unresolved (the permanent entry id decides) and for a NOOP event (at most one extra visible, resolvable entry is tolerated and the age alert fires). (S-manifest) FU-AC-119 is a parent over individually identified scenarios S01 to S26 listed in queue_migration_scenarios.json; the evidence is one result per id and the aggregator FAILS when any id is missing or has no result. (S25) Deletion fence: delete an account, remove the policy as specified, then attempt direct SDK create, update and delete with a previously issued token and delayed writes: all refused, no document recreated. (S26) Trigger failure: force the trigger to fail through its whole retry lifecycle, deliver a second divergent write: the watchdog quarantines the surviving snapshot, a gap record and the alert exist, the owner sees the gap in the inventory and the export, and the recovery tool restores the earlier snapshot within the point-in-time window. (18b) No-op rule: separately change notes, change status and remove one set in a legacy snapshot while all other fields stay identical: each produces an unresolved quarantine entry; none is ignored. (12) Enter `DRAIN` with the verified flush unavailable or without the minimum-version gate or without a device registry: the account stays out of (or in) `DRAIN` and nothing is denied. Fails if any set is lost or doubled, a legacy write is denied before `SEALED`, or a quarantined write changes canonical state without a user command.
